verdict.summary: A multi-tenant AI agent that uses connected users' Strava data is prohibited under Strava's current API Policy. The prohibition covers operating an AI application, including grounding and derived data, even with user consent. Ordinary OAuth app review is an athlete-capacity gate and does not change the stated AI restriction. Strava MCP is also limited to a subscriber's personal, non-commercial use.
verdict.activeEffort: Not applicable for the proposed AI integration: the current policy prohibits using Strava API Materials or Strava Data in an AI Application. A conventional non-AI OAuth integration would require implementation and review materials.
verdict.waitTime: Unknown: no official or community figure was found for a policy determination about the AI Application prohibition; ordinary app review is typically 7–10 business days after the 10-athlete threshold.
verdict.mainGate: Strava prohibits API Materials and Strava Data in the development, training, evaluation, or operation of an AI Application.

recommendation.text: Do not use Strava OAuth or Strava Data in this multi-tenant AI agent. If Strava supplies written permission, treat it as a bespoke approval: use one registered OAuth application with per-athlete tokens, submit the exact approved architecture for review after reaching the athlete threshold, and keep Strava data outside any AI system unless the permission explicitly says otherwise.

essentials.text: Use OAuth authorization-code exchange. Access tokens expire after six hours; retain each athlete's refresh token securely, refresh with grant_type=refresh_token, and atomically replace it because the old refresh token is immediately invalidated.

sources.quote: Access tokens expire six hours after they are created, so they must be refreshed in order for an application to maintain access to a user's resources.
To refresh an access token, applications should call the POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token endpoint, specifying grant_type: refresh_token
Once a new refresh token is returned, the older refresh token is invalidated immediately.

essentials.text: Send web users to https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize and configure a callback domain that contains every production redirect URI. localhost and 127.0.0.1 are allow-listed for local development.

sources.quote: Web applications Redirect the user to GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize .
Must be within the callback domain specified by the application. localhost and 127.0.0.1 are white-listed.

essentials.text: New applications start in Single Player Mode, where only the developer's Strava account can authenticate. The dashboard can self-serve an expansion to 10 athletes; beyond that, additional athletes cannot authenticate until review approval.

sources.quote: All new applications start in single-player mode. This is the default state where only your own Strava account can authenticate with the app
This raises your access to: Athlete capacity of 10
Until your app has been reviewed, you won't be able to authenticate any additional athletes to your app.

essentials.text: Default limits are 200 requests per 15 minutes and 2,000 per day overall, plus 100 non-upload requests per 15 minutes and 1,000 per day. At the 10-athlete tier, published limits are 400 overall requests per 15 minutes and 4,000 per day, plus 200 read requests per 15 minutes and 2,000 per day.

sources.quote: The default overall rate limit allows 200 requests every 15 minutes, with up to 2,000 requests per day.
The default "non-upload" rate limit allows 100 requests every 15 minutes, with up to 1,000 requests per day.
Overall rate limits: 400 requests / 15min & 4,000 requests / day
Read read limits: 200 requests / 15min & 2,000 requests / day

essentials.text: Strava API access is currently provided at no charge, although Strava reserves the right to charge later. A Strava subscription is required to register an app; its price was not found in the researched sources.

Strava reserves the right to charge you for use of the Strava API Materials and access to the Strava Platform

steps.title: Request a written policy determination before registering an AI integration

detail.text: Email developers@strava.com with questions about the policy and the proposed architecture. Under the current policy, do not use Strava API Materials or Strava Data in the development, training, evaluation, or operation of an AI Application.

sources.quote: You may not use the Strava API Materials or Strava Data, directly or indirectly, in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application.
You can reach out to developers@strava.com, or post your question on the Developer Forums .

steps.title: Prepare the permission request architecture summary

detail.text: Use this draft to request a written determination, replacing bracketed fields with the real architecture before sending it to Strava.

steps.output:
Subject: Request for written determination — AI agent and Strava OAuth

We operate a multi-tenant AI agent for end users. Proposed flow: each athlete authorizes our registered OAuth app; our service reads only [scopes]; [describe exactly whether any Strava field reaches an LLM, embedding store, tool call, log, or vendor]. Data is isolated per athlete and deleted on request. Please confirm in writing whether this architecture is permitted under the API Policy, and identify any required restrictions or review path.

steps.title: Prepare OAuth callback checks for any expressly permitted implementation

detail.text: Use this checklist only for a conventional non-AI implementation that is permitted under Strava's policy and has reached the implementation stage.

sources.quote: code is short lived and can only be used once.
Applications should check which scopes a user has accepted.

steps.output:
OAuth callback checklist
- Authorization URL: https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize
- Production redirect host is inside the configured callback domain.
- Local callback uses localhost or 127.0.0.1 only.
- Exchange each authorization code once; do not retry a consumed code.
- Store refresh tokens per athlete and atomically replace them on refresh.
- Verify accepted scopes before enabling features.

steps.title: Do not submit ordinary app review as a workaround for the AI prohibition

detail.text: Ordinary Developer Program review is an athlete-capacity gate and does not change the API Policy's AI restriction.

sources.quote: If you want to scale beyond 10 connected athletes you’ll need to submit your app for review .
You may not use the Strava API Materials or Strava Data, directly or indirectly, in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application.

detail.text: Do not deploy Strava Data in an AI agent under the current policy. For a separately permitted non-AI app, restrict each athlete's data to that athlete, enforce seven-day cache limits, and provide written deletion confirmation.

sources.quote: Strava Data provided by a specific Strava user may be displayed or disclosed in your Developer Application only to that user.
You may not retain Strava Data in your cache for longer than seven (7) days.
You must also provide the user with written confirmation of successful deletion.

gotchas.text: User consent does not make AI use permissible, and the restriction also covers derived, aggregated, anonymized, and generated data.

sources.quote: even if a user of your Developer Application consents.
Any data derived from, aggregated from, anonymized from, or generated using Strava Data

gotchas.text: Do not place Strava Data or derivatives in embeddings, vector databases, search indexes, or knowledge graphs: persistent indexes are expressly prohibited.

sources.quote: You may not store Strava Data, or any data derived from Strava Data, in any Persistent Index.

gotchas.text: Strava MCP is not an alternative for a commercial multi-tenant agent because it is limited to a subscriber's personal data and may not enable commercial or third-party access.

sources.quote: The Strava MCP is the sole authorized first-party agent-mediated interface
The Strava MCP is not authorized for, and may not be used to enable, any commercial or third-party access

gotchas.text: Do not share or multiplex OAuth credentials: store credentials per athlete and per app.

sources.quote: share, transfer, multiplex, or otherwise re-use API Tokens or authentication credentials across multiple servers
